Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Holdings Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for the question-and-queue will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Holdings Inc.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. With me this morning are Johnathan Reed, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Kim, Chief Credit Officer; and Elena Vargas, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Reed.

Johnathan Reed:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Holdings Inc. delivered excellent results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Expanding our market share
2. Improving our efficiency ratio
3. Strengthening our balance sheet
4. Investing in our people
5. Driving innovation
6. Meeting our ESG goals.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key performance areas. We saw resilient non-interest income despite choppy markets, disciplined management of our risk-weighted assets, prudent reserve positioning with strong coverage ratios, meaningful progress on our efficiency ratio, robust deposit growth across a favorable mix, and technology investments delivering clear efficiency gains. These results position us well for continued execution.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Holdings Inc. reported net income of $1.5 billion for the third quarter, or $2.35 per diluted share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 9% year-over-year due to higher interest rates, solid loan growth, and favorable deposit mix dynamics. Non-interest income was $2.8 billion for the quarter, up 12% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This performance was driven by strength in investment banking fees, wealth management, and payments, even amidst moderating inflation, ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Ukraine, and signals from the Federal Reserve of potential rate cuts later this year. Our efficiency ratio improved to 54.8%, reflecting operational leverage from our efficiency initiatives. We are on track to achieve our financial targets for the year.

Let me dive deeper into our non-interest income performance, which underscores our diversified fee-based revenue model. Investment banking and capital markets fees contributed $1.1 billion, or 39% of the total, up 22% year-over-year. This was propelled by a rebound in M&A activity, with private equity dry powder surpassing $2.5 trillion globally. We advised on 15 deals exceeding $1 billion, including a $12 billion acquisition in the midstream energy sector. Debt underwriting fees rose 18% to $450 million, supported by investment-grade issuance volumes of $450 billion year-to-date—the strongest since 2021. Equity underwriting was flat due to a slower IPO pipeline, with only 45 U.S. IPOs in the quarter versus 75 last year, amid high valuations and election uncertainty. Moderate volatility, with the VIX averaging 15.2, boosted our structured products desk by $120 million.

Trading income came in at $650 million, down 8% year-over-year, as lower volatility led to range-bound trading in fixed income and equities. Our FICC desk experienced compression from a modestly steepening U.S. Treasury yield curve, with 10-year yields at 4.35%, reducing client flow volumes by 10%. Equities trading dipped 5% with S&P 500 gains of 4% quarter-over-quarter. We offset this with $80 million in gains from our macro hedge book in short-duration positions anticipating Fed cuts, and deployed our proprietary AI-driven algorithmic trading platform, UniFlow AI, which cut execution costs by 15% and captured 2% higher spreads in FX pairs.

Wealth and asset management fees were a standout at $680 million, up 15% year-over-year, on $1.2 trillion in assets under management, which grew 9% from $25 billion in net inflows. Positive equity markets, with the MSCI World Index up 6%, lifted performance fees 25%, especially in alternatives where private credit AUM reached $180 billion. Advisory fees benefited from wealth transfer trends, projected at $84 trillion over the next two decades. North America led with 18% growth, while EMEA grew 7% despite MiFID II headwinds.

Card and payments fees hit $210 million, up 10%, supported by resilient consumer spending at 3.5% core PCE inflation. Interchange from co-branded Visa cards grew 12% on 8% volume increase, though margins slipped to 2.1% from regulatory pressures. Treasury services added $160 million, flat year-over-year.

Regionally, North America drove 65% of growth, Asia-Pacific surged 25% to $450 million from China reopening and ASEAN M&A like a $5 billion Singapore tech deal, while Europe grew 3% amid Basel IV and ECB rate expectations. Non-interest income now comprises 42% of total revenue, up from 38% two years ago. Initiatives include a $500 million fintech accelerator with Stripe and Adyen, and $90 million in ESG advisory from green bonds. We guide to $11.0 to $11.5 billion full-year, assuming S&P volatility under 18 and M&A 10% above 2023 levels.

Next, on risk-weighted assets management, a key element of our capital optimization. Our total RWAs stood at $1.18 trillion at quarter-end, up 2.1% quarter-over-quarter but flat year-over-year. This reflects balanced growth offset by derisking. Credit RWAs at $968 billion, 82% of total, rose 3%; market RWAs at $105 billion were stable; operational RWAs at $107 billion dipped 1%.

Credit growth came from CIB and consumer portfolios. CIB RWAs up 4.2% to $420 billion on $15 billion new commitments in acquisition finance. Risk weights steady at 65% with PD at 1.8%. Consumer RWAs grew 2.5% to $380 billion from mortgage originations, weights at 35%. CRE RWAs up 5% to $168 billion, weights to 120% aligning with Basel III Endgame; we stress-tested our $25 billion office portfolio.

Market RWAs benefited from lower VaR post-volatility drop, down 2% with PRA model approvals. Operational decline from AI-driven loss estimates.

North America RWAs up 3.5% to $530 billion; Europe flat at $355 billion after derisking NPLs via a €5 billion sale; APAC up 5% to $235 billion; emerging markets steady.

Optimizations included model refinements shaving 2.5% off credit RWAs, $10 billion securitizations for 15% relief, RWA Engine 2.0 identifying $20 billion low-return assets, and SA-CCR reducing derivatives RWAs by $4 billion. RWA density improved to 43.5%, capital velocity at 4.2x.

We're targeting high-RoRA growth in renewables and tech, capping CRE, with potential $15 billion capital release over 2025-2027.

Turning to reserve dynamics, we recorded a $450 million provision credit this quarter, year-to-date build of $1.1 billion versus $2.8 billion last year. Under CECL, anchored to 300+ macro variables via our Global Economic Scenario Generator, this reflects improving loss rates—criticized loans down 15% to $18.5 billion, charge-offs at $320 million annualized 0.35%, delinquencies at 1.2% consumer and 0.9% commercial.

Macro tailwinds: unemployment at 4.1%, GDP at 2.6%. CRE cap rates compressed in multifamily; office build of $120 million on $4.2 billion exposure.

Coverage remains strong: ACL at 1.28% of loans or $12.4 billion, 285% of NPLs, 112% of criticized—above peers. Non-accrual at 0.45%.

U.S. consumer FICOs at 735, Europe release on energy loans, APAC selective. GenAI with Palantir cut model times 70%, accuracy to R²=0.92. Guidance $800 million to $1.2 billion full-year provisions.

On efficiency ratio progress, ours improved to 54.8% in Q3, down 320 bps year-over-year, full-year 56.2%—best since 2019. Outperforms peers.

Driven by 2.1% expense growth to $4.2 billion via RPA saving $180 million, versus 8.4% revenue growth to $7.7 billion on 25 bps NIM expansion to 3.45%, deposit beta 32%.

Consumer banking at 52.1% with branch optimization; CIB 57.3%; wealth 48.9%. U.S. 53.2%, EMEA 59.8%, APAC 61.4%.

Core modernization on Temenos slashed mainframe costs 28%; GenAI fraud detection saved $220 million; STP 95%+.

Targets: 53-55% 2024, sub-52% 2025, below 50% 2027, supporting 12-14% ROTCE.

Deposit growth totaled $285 billion, up 4.2% quarter-over-quarter, 11.8% year-over-year—10th straight quarter. Core organic $248 billion up 3.8%, L/D 82%.

Transactional $112 billion, 39%, 15 bps cost, 94% retention via Treasury platform. Savings $128 billion, 45%, up 6.1%, FlexSave Pro inflows. Time $45 billion, 16%, 4.60% cost.

Beta 48%, top clients <5%. Southeast/Texas led; digital AI personalization up conversions 25%; OneBank cross-sell; pricing discipline. Q4 growth 3-4%, NIM to 3.55%.

Finally, technology investments of $1.2 billion, 8% of opex, drove cost-to-income to 54.2%. Cloud migration 75% done, $180 million savings, STP 98.5%. AI fraud prevented $450 million, credit times to 48 hours. RPA automated 65%, 1,200 FTEs. FY2024 $1.4 billion more for GenAI, quantum security. 3.2x ROI, $500 million EBIT unlock.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring geopolitical tensions and regulatory changes like Basel IV. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, building on our RWA discipline.

David Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loans at 0.45% and delinquencies at 1.05%. Coverage ratios are peer-leading at 285% on NPLs. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for queuing questions via telephone or webcast will be given momentarily. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the outlook for non-interest income given ongoing market volatility and potential rate cuts?

Johnathan Reed:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. As Michael outlined, we're guiding $11.0 to $11.5 billion full-year, assuming volatility under 18 and M&A tracking 10% above 2023. Risks like prolonged high rates or recession could pressure fees 5-7%, but our diversification—42% of revenue—and initiatives like the fintech accelerator position us resiliently. We're leaning into ESG and embedded payments for growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee:
What is your strategy for deposit growth and mix amid potential rate cuts?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Mike. Our strategy centers on digital acquisition, relationship deepening, and pricing discipline to sustain 4-6% organic growth. Transactional remains sticky at 39%, savings the engine despite beta moderation, and we're shifting time deposits shorter. Expect 3-4% Q4 growth, funding NIM expansion without wholesale reliance. AI personalization and partnerships like Plaid are key uplift drivers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
How are you addressing RWA growth in light of Basel IV implementation?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, Sarah. We're proactively optimizing through model refinements, securitizations, and portfolio tools like RWA Engine 2.0, delivering 150 bps density improvement. Regionally derisking CRE and NPLs while growing high-RoRA areas. Basel IV output floor from 2025 is in our models; we're positioned for capital release via buybacks, maintaining CET1 above 13%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with Citi. Please go ahead.

David Wong:
Can you update us on reserve builds and coverage ratios, particularly in CRE?

David Kim:
Sure, David. The $450 million release this quarter reflects improving loss emergence and macro, with ACL 1.28% of loans, 285% NPLs, 112% criticized—above peers. CRE office exposure $4.2 billion prudently reserved; overall we're covered for recession scenarios. Forward $800 million to $1.2 billion provisions, focusing derisking legacy while scaling equipment finance and ESG.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Reed for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Reed:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Holdings Inc. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Reserve build/release: rationale and coverage ratios
Deposit growth and mix (transactional, savings, time deposits): trends and strategies
Technology investments and their impact on efficiency

aspect_summary.Reserve build/release: rationale and cov: $450M provision credit (YTD build $1.1B vs $2.8B prior year) due to improving loss rates (criticized -15% to $18.5B, charge-offs 0.35%, delinq 1.05%), favorable macro (unemp 4.1%, GDP 2.6%), CECL models; ACL 1.28% of loans ($12.4B), 285% NPLs (0.45%), 112% criticized; FY provisions $800M-$1.2B.
aspect_summary.Efficiency ratio: progress and targets: Improved to 54.8% Q3 (-320bps YoY), FY 56.2% (best since 2019) via 2.1% expense growth vs 8.4% revenue growth, RPA savings $180M; targets 53-55% 2024, sub-52% 2025, <50% 2027, supporting 12-14% ROTCE.
